record.paper_title: Open Questions on Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics of Chemical Reaction Networks
record.original_question: How can chemical reaction networks be coarse-grained in a thermodynamically consistent way when resolving every elementary reaction is impractical for biochemical applications, especially for transient effects and for complex networks such as genetic networks, while preserving the ability of stochastic thermodynamics to assess thermodynamic costs?

evidence.quote: Thermodynamically consistent coarse graining is a crucial challenge for thermodynamics of CRNs. Indeed, the need to resolve elementary reactions is a priori a severe practical limitation for biochemical applications. Fortunately, important results have been obtained (at steady state) showing for instance that ST can be straightforwardly applied to describe non-elementary reactions catalyzed by cytosolic enzymes. This is very good news for studies on metabolism, but more work is needed to consider transient effects and find out if ST could also be used to assess the cost of more complex networks such as genetic ones.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a chemical reaction network (CRN) modeled at the level of elementary reactions, equipped with the framework of stochastic thermodynamics: each elementary reaction has well-defined forward and reverse rates satisfying local detailed balance, so that thermodynamic quantities such as entropy production, dissipated work, and free-energy changes can be assigned consistently to individual trajectories and to ensemble averages. In many biochemical settings (e.g., enzyme-catalyzed metabolic pathways, signaling cascades, gene regulatory networks), resolving every elementary step is impractical, and one wishes to replace the network by a coarse-grained CRN whose nodes are effective species and whose edges are effective (non-elementary) reactions with effective rate laws.

Formulate and develop a general coarse-graining procedure that, given an elementary CRN together with a partition or projection onto a reduced set of species and reactions, produces a reduced CRN satisfying the following requirements:

1. (Steady-state consistency) At nonequilibrium steady state, the entropy production rate, the chemical affinities along cycles, and the dissipated work computed from the coarse-grained CRN agree exactly with those of the underlying elementary CRN.

2. (Transient consistency) Beyond steady state, the coarse-grained dynamics reproduce — exactly or with controlled error bounds — the time-dependent entropy production, free-energy dissipation, and fluctuation relations of stochastic thermodynamics during transients.

3. (Applicability to complex networks) The procedure extends beyond cytosolic enzymatic catalysis to networks involving multiple time scales, allosteric regulation, and templated polymerization, in particular to genetic networks (transcription, translation, and gene regulation), so that thermodynamic costs of information processing in such networks can be quantified.

Provide either an explicit construction meeting (1)–(3), or prove obstructions identifying which classes of elementary CRNs admit such thermodynamically consistent coarse grainings and which do not.
artifact.category_tag: stochastic thermodynamics of chemical reaction networks
artifact.status_search_result: Thermodynamically consistent coarse graining of CRNs has been established at steady state for cytosolic enzymatic catalysis (Wachtel–Rao–Esposito 2018, extending Michaelis–Menten reductions), and partial results exist for photo-isomerization and information-theoretic reductions of gene networks. However, a general procedure that is exact for transient regimes and applicable to complex networks such as genetic ones remains an active research direction without a complete solution.

status_evidence.title: Thermodynamically Consistent Coarse Graining of Biocatalysts beyond Michaelis–Menten
status_evidence.snippet: A coarse-graining procedure that captures the entropy-production rate of the underlying catalytic mechanism; exact at steady state, approximate in transients.
status_evidence.claim: Steady-state thermodynamically consistent coarse graining is solved for biocatalysts.

status_evidence.title: Coarse graining photo-isomerization reactions: Thermodynamic consistency
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work extends thermodynamically consistent coarse graining to photo-isomerization and molecular ratchets.
status_evidence.claim: Extensions beyond enzymatic catalysis are still being developed.

status_evidence.title: Information Thermodynamics and Reducibility of Large Gene Networks
status_evidence.snippet: Studies reducibility of gene regulatory networks from an information-thermodynamic perspective.
status_evidence.claim: Coarse graining of genetic networks with thermodynamic cost accounting is partial and ongoing.

status_evidence.title: Thermodynamically Consistent Coarse-graining (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent preprint addressing thermodynamic consistency in coarse graining procedures.
status_evidence.claim: The general problem remains under active investigation in 2025.
